audits.claim: Deleting cached data on the event-type Advanced tab leaves the connected-calendar cache status and deletion action stale because the mutation does not refetch the query.
audits.evidence: For an owned Google credential with cached data, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:17-30 verifies ownership and deletes its cache rows. packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42-50 only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback, whereas EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-384 supplies no onChanged callback. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:152-160 disables focus refetch and :183 forwards only props.onChanged; neither this path nor the query-client configuration in packages/trpc/react/trpc.ts:99-123 installs mutation-driven invalidation. Consequently the existing cacheUpdatedAt prop still satisfies hasCache at CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:67-69 and renders the old timestamp and Delete cached data item at :82-110, although a fresh connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-35 query would return null for the deleted rows.

audits.claim: The error-state calendar remove action now respects disableConnectionModification, so it disappears on the event-type Advanced tab.
audits.evidence: A credential whose listCalendars call throws is returned without calendars by packages/lib/CalendarManager.ts:73,112-135 and reaches the Alert branch of SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:108-134. That branch now forwards disableConnectionModification at :130, and CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:68,114 suppresses disconnection when it is true; EventAdvancedTab.tsx:375 explicitly sets it to true. The supplied diff confirms the old Alert branch ignored this flag, so the behavioral change is real, but it makes the error branch obey the same connection-modification restriction as the healthy branch rather than establishing a broken recovery flow. Removal remains available in the general calendar-management screen: apps/web/components/apps/CalendarListContainer.tsx:112-117 uses the same wrapper without the disabling prop.

audits.claim: The migration initializes legacy cache rows with the migration timestamp, which the new dropdown presents as their last cache update, and its warning comment incorrectly says there is no default.
audits.evidence: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 adds updatedAt with NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so an existing row containing availability fetched before migration receives the migration transaction timestamp without refreshing its value; the warning at :4 contradicts that SQL. packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-186 takes the maximum updatedAt for the credential, connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-35 forwards it unchanged, and CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:82-94 renders it as Last updated. Thus a legacy Google cache displayed before its next write has an inaccurate diagnostic timestamp, but the migration does not change the cached value or expiry, and ordinary upserts at calendar-cache.repository.ts:150-168 subsequently update the timestamp through schema.prisma:1719. This is a one-time, low-impact status-label inaccuracy rather than a demonstrated availability or data-loss defect.
